comment: How scripts/conformance-reports.mjs runs each implementation. Build the adapter first (see its README). env values may use ~ for the home directory. executionArgs are extra kit options for the execution run. notes are hand-written and shown, labelled as such, on the implementation's page.

notes: The differential scripts check graphql-js against the references more broadly than the kit's vectors, and document where it departs from the draft: [lexer and parser](../scripts/differential-lexer.mjs) (`KNOWN`), [validation](../scripts/differential-validation.mjs) (`DISCREPANCIES`), [coercion](../scripts/differential-coercion.mjs) (`KNOWN`) and [type system](../scripts/differential-type-system.mjs) (`VALIDATION_DEVIATIONS`).
Behaviour outside the kit's fixtures is described in the README's [What graphql-js does](../README.md#what-graphql-js-does).

The differential scripts check graphql-js against the references more broadly than the kit's vectors, and document where it departs from the draft: [lexer and parser](../scripts/differential-lexer.mjs) (`KNOWN`), [validation](../scripts/differential-validation.mjs) (`DISCREPANCIES`), [coercion](../scripts/differential-coercion.mjs) (`KNOWN`) and [type system](../scripts/differential-type-system.mjs) (`VALIDATION_DEVIATIONS`).
Behaviour outside the kit's fixtures is described in the README's [What graphql-js does](../README.md#what-graphql-js-does).

The sheet runs the adapter with `--validate`: coerce validates each document first, as `GraphQL.execute` always does, so invalid documents are graded under `invalidNotExecuted` (§6.1.1). graphql-java isn't built to execute unvalidated documents.

graphql-java uses each subscription event as the root field's value and calls no resolver on it, so the source stream's emission of an event stands for the root field's call (in execution, and in coerce's `subscription-source`). `parentValue` at a subscription's root therefore says nothing about graphql-java, and a stream cancelled while an event executes can't catch graphql-java mid-event.
Introspection runs with graphql-java's Good Faith Introspection turned off per request (its documented switch); with it on, graphql-java refuses the kit's full introspection queries.
Not claimed: `coordinate` (graphql-java has no schema coordinate parser or resolver; `FieldCoordinates` is a type and field name pair), `deferred-items` and `exact-numbers`.
Every finding, with source locations and reproductions, is described in the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-java/README.md).

The adapter uses async-graphql's dynamic schema API (`async_graphql::dynamic`). Every execution finding comes from `async_graphql::dynamic`, which the derive-macro API doesn't use: resolver errors without a path, any error nulling all of `data`, a null list item completed as an object, fields resolved once per selection (a mutation root field twice), fragments on a union not applied, an integer ID passed through as a number, fragments at the subscription root ignored, and a response stream that ends after any event with an error. The derive API may behave differently; it does stop an error at a nullable field. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/async-graphql/README.md#known-async-graphql-deviations).

A source stream's failure can only be an error item in a Rust stream: async-graphql answers it with an error result, then completes the response stream normally, which the kit accepts as completing with that error (the weaker reading of §6.2.3, so `failsWithSource` passes). At a subscription's root the event is the root field's value, so `parentValue` grades nothing there.
The adapter doesn't claim `uncoercible-results`, so `intFraction` is untested here, not passed. It claims only the execution area; async-graphql has no schema coordinate API.

The sheet runs the adapter with `--idle`, which claims `idle` by waiting for .NET's thread pool to go quiet: runtime behaviour, not something Hot Chocolate promises. The kit's determinism replay passed, and a run without `--idle` (grace-based, random runs only) found the same failures. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/hotchocolate/README.md).

The sheet also passes `--introspection-list-depth 2`, which raises Hot Chocolate's own introspection depth limit (`ValidationOptions`); with the default, Hot Chocolate refuses the kit's full introspection queries. Hot Chocolate names `__Type.isOneOf` `oneOf`, so introspect is graded against September 2025. For validate only, the adapter builds the kit's schema with `StrictValidation = false`, because Hot Chocolate refuses an interface with no implementation; that option affects schema checks, not document validation. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/hotchocolate/README.md).

With `parent-values`, a subscription root field reports the event message as its parent: Hot Chocolate keeps the operation's root value as the parent there and hands the resolver the event as the event message, which is the field's value by default. So `parentValue` grades only below a subscription's root, as docs/conformance.md prescribes for such engines.
Every finding is described, with source locations and a minimal reproduction, in the [adapter's README](../adapters/hotchocolate/README.md#known-hot-chocolate-deviations).

The `mutation` finding is graphql-core 3.2's `execute_fields_serially`, which calls every root field's resolver in a plain loop and only chains the awaiting. Resolvers written as `async def` don't start until awaited, so they run in order; resolvers that return a future or task (a DataLoader's `load`, `create_task`) and synchronous resolvers with side effects run early. graphql-core 3.3 chains the calls, as graphql-js does. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-core/README.md).

The `nothingAfterCancel` finding (a SHOULD) is graphql-core's `MapAsyncIterator`: closing the response stream doesn't stop an event already executing, whose result is still delivered (`subscription/map_async_iterator.py`). graphql-js 16 does the same.

The coerce run executes without validating, as the graphql-js adapter does. Every request error graphql-core returns, a document that doesn't parse included, carries `"data": null`, because `ExecutionResult.formatted` always writes `data`; the kit counts that under `requestErrorNoData` (§7.1.3). The adapter passes graphql-core's own answer through, so the introspect area's syntax-error case fails `executes` for the same reason.
Claimed: `coordinate`, through graphql-core's `parse_schema_coordinate` and `resolve_ast_schema_coordinate`, and `subscription-stream`, through `subscribe`.

The sheet runs graphql-ruby with `--invalid-results`: a schema that uses graphql-ruby's documented `type_error` and `rescue_from` hooks. Out of the box, a resolver result of the wrong shape (a non-list for a list, an object for an Int, a runtime type that isn't a possible type) or one its type can't represent (a non-finite Float, an unknown enum value) raises out of `execute` instead of becoming a field error (§6.4.4), so the client gets no response at all. The sheet's `resultCoercion` pass depends on the hooks; without them the adapter answers `no-response` and the kit counts these against `responds` and `resultCoercion`.

The `intFraction` finding (a MUST) is graphql-ruby's Int coercion, which calls `to_i`, so `1.2` becomes `1`, with or without the hooks. Boolean is `!!value`, so an object becomes `true` instead of an error: the `booleanResult` fixture's `dataMatches` and `nullsExplained` finding. The kit doesn't send strings such as `"false"` for a Boolean, since §3.5.4 lets a service coerce other values "where reasonable". See the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-ruby/README.md).

graphql-ruby validates before executing, and documents running an invalid document with `validate: false` as undefined, so the sheet's coerce run validates first and grades invalid documents under `invalidNotExecuted` (§6.1.1), or `onlyValidExecuted` where graphql-ruby's validator lets them through. graphql-ruby's validate results use its defaults, including the `allow_legacy_*` settings that only log a warning; see the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-ruby/README.md).

graphql-ruby's subscriptions have no source stream: the subscribe step is an ordinary execution of the operation, and each event re-executes it. So `subscription-stream` isn't claimed, and coerce's `subscription-source` uses a `GraphQL::Subscriptions` subclass that delivers one event; an error raised in the subscribe step comes back as a field error with `data`, not the request error September 2026 asks for (`sourceStreamError`).
Not claimed: `coordinate`. graphql-ruby has no schema coordinate parser; `Schema.find` takes its own dotted path syntax, not §2.14's coordinates.
Introspection is graded against September 2025: graphql-ruby rejects September 2026's query (no `includeDeprecated` on `__Schema.directives`).

graphql-go doesn't make runs deterministic (it resolves fields in Go map order), so the adapter doesn't claim `idle` and the kit waits 10 ms after each settle instead; the sheet's cases are random runs only.

The resolver returns a thunk, graphql-go's way to keep several resolvers pending. The Non-Null propagation and mutation ordering findings come from thunks; with `--sync` only the key order, leaf coercion, mutation error and subscription stream findings remain. Under `--strict`, key order (a SHOULD) fails most `leaves` and `ordering` cases by itself, since graphql-go writes keys sorted. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-go/README.md#known-graphql-go-deviations).

Subscription streams: graphql-go's source stream is a `chan interface{}`, which can't carry an error, so a failing source ends the response stream normally (`failsWithSource`); a client cancels through the request's context, and an event still executing then yields a `context canceled` error without a path (`nothingAfterCancel`, `errorPath`). The adapter doesn't claim `custom-scalar-results` (a graphql-go `SerializeFn` has no error result).

graphql-go has no SDL builder, so for introspect and coerce the adapter builds a `graphql.Schema` from graphql-go's own parse of the SDL, one to one, and refuses what graphql-go can't express (interfaces implementing interfaces, `repeatable`, schema descriptions, deprecated arguments and input fields, `@specifiedBy`, `@oneOf`, extensions other than `extend type`); the kit grades those as crashes. graphql-go's parser follows October 2016 (no `null` literal, no descriptions on executable definitions, no empty selection sets); its introspection is October 2021's, so the kit grades September 2025's query without newer fields; a request error is written with `"data": null` (`requestErrorNoData`); and 19 coerce vectors with `1e400` get no response because Go's `encoding/json` refuses the number before graphql-go sees it. The adapter doesn't claim `validate`: the kit's validation schemas use interfaces implementing interfaces and `repeatable`, both in October 2021, which graphql-go 0.8.1 can't express, so 3215 of 3354 vectors would grade its schema model rather than its rules (rule gaps seen on the rest are in the README). Nor `schema` or `coordinate` (no SDL builder, no schema coordinate API).

The adapter uses graphql-dotnet's schema-first `Schema.For`, its default `DocumentExecuter` and the System.Text.Json serializer. List items are `IDataLoaderResult` values, the only kind of item graphql-dotnet waits for. `idle` holds because everything runs on one thread, the kit-driven subscription source stream included; the determinism replay passed.

Execution: `resultCoercion`, because `FloatGraphType` passes a non-finite double through and `GraphQLSerializer` then throws, so the client gets no response; the `subscriptionAlias` fixture, which graphql-dotnet refuses at validation because its single-root-field rule counts selections rather than response names; and `errorLocationsPresent` (SHOULD), because a field selected twice is merged into a `GraphQLField` that can't hold a location. `coerce` isn't implemented for this adapter, and graphql-dotnet has no schema coordinate API, so neither area is claimed.

`schema-extensions` is claimed, but `SchemaBuilder` applies only `extend type`, and drops every other kind of extension without an error, so the rules about them are not enforced. graphql-dotnet rejects the kit's full introspection queries: it has no `specifiedByURL`, input-value deprecation is behind an experimental flag that is off by default, and `isRepeatable` needs that kind of flag and is also hidden by the default schema filter. The kit then discovers which fields exist and grades the rest under the September 2025 profile. The default schema filter also hides every directive with a type system location from `__schema.directives`. Every finding is described with source locations in the [adapter's README](../adapters/graphql-dotnet/README.md#known-graphql-dotnet-deviations).

Juniper builds schemas from Rust types. The adapter uses its documented dynamic route, a hand-written `GraphQLType` with `TypeInfo`, and Juniper's own code completes objects, lists and scalars. Values a typed schema can't hold aren't sent: uncoercible results only for Float (`uncoercibleTypes`), so `intFraction` is untested, no `scalar-results` (an ID is a string type, an Int an `i32`), no `custom-scalar-results` (a Juniper scalar's output can't fail), and no null for a Non-Null list item or subscription event (`nullItems: false`). The report's provenance counts what was left out.

Fields called twice (a mutation root field too, `mutationFieldsOnce`; repeated errors at one path, `errorPathsUnique`; a null lost when results merge), error paths without list indices, the nested list, the non-finite Float and the subscription findings reproduce with `#[graphql_object]` (`examples/macros.rs`). A source stream's failure can only be an error item in a Rust stream, which Juniper answers with an error result and a normal completion; the kit accepts that as completing with the error (the weaker reading of §6.2.3), so `failsWithSource` passes. See the [adapter's README](../adapters/juniper/README.md#known-juniper-deviations).

The adapter doesn't claim `invalid-results` (result shapes are fixed by Rust types), `custom-directives` (Juniper can't declare a directive of its own), `parse-sdl` (Juniper parses only executable documents), or the schema and coordinate areas (Juniper doesn't read SDL and has no schema coordinate API, so every schema verdict would be the adapter's). Introspection descriptions are read from SDL by the adapter with `async-graphql-parser`, which can't read September 2025's string forms: those 3 vectors aren't graded.

The adapter tests `com.apollographql.apollo:apollo-execution` 5.2.0. It builds an `ExecutableSchema` from the SDL with one `Resolver` on every field, and runs each request as a server does: the body goes through `parseAsGraphQLRequest`, and the response is `GraphQLResponse#serialize`'s JSON. `idle` holds because every coroutine runs on the adapter's own single-threaded dispatcher; the determinism replay passed. apollo-execution uses each subscription event as the root field's value and calls no resolver on it, so the source stream's emission of an event stands for the root field's call, and `parentValue` grades nothing at a subscription's root.

Execution findings: `resultCoercion`, because an unknown enum value is passed through, and a non-finite Float reaches Apollo's JSON writer, which throws, so the client gets no response. `serialErrorsKept`, because field errors live in the result tree and a propagating Non-Null error drops the ones already there. `dataMatches`, because a subscription event doesn't propagate a null Non-Null root field. `errorLocationsPresent` (SHOULD), because execution errors carry no locations.

apollo-execution has no public validation function. For validate, the adapter reads the verdict that `ExecutableSchema#execute` hands to its `PersistedDocumentCache`, and stops the request there. apollo-ast reports Lone Anonymous Operation and All Variables Used as Apollo-specific warnings, which apollo-execution drops, and has no Single Root Field rule. Every request error carries `"data": null` because `GraphQLResponse#serialize` always writes it; the kit counts that under `requestErrorNoData` in most coerce vectors. apollo-ast's schema validation says it doesn't implement the full rules, and interface cycles crash its cache key computation.
The introspection types lack `__Type.isOneOf`, so introspect is graded against September 2025, and `__type` with an unknown name raises instead of returning null.

Not claimed: `deferred-items` (apollo-execution doesn't await list items), `exact-numbers` (Apollo's JSON reader reads a number beyond a `Long` as a `Double`) and `unvalidated` (`execute` always validates). Every finding, with source locations and reproductions, is in the [adapter's README](../adapters/apollo-kotlin/README.md#known-apollo-kotlin-deviations).
